p1.original: 4.1 经典条件反射为联结式学习提供了解释，即一个能够引发内在反射的刺激如何与另一个先天中性的刺激建立联结，使得后者能引发与前者相同的反应。
p1.en: 4.1 The classic reflection provides an explanation of how a synergetic learning can be linked to another innate incentive that triggers an inherent reflection, so that the latter can trigger the same reaction as the former.

p2.original: 4.2 在操作性条件反射中，某一行为引发的奖赏和惩罚等后果影响着该行为再次出现的概率。
p2.en: 4.2 In the reflection of operational conditions, consequences such as rewards and penalties arising from an act affect the probability of the act being repeated.

p3.original: 4.3 在认知心理学看来，某些形式的学习只能解释为心理过程的改变，而不仅仅是行为本身的改变。
p3.en: 4.3 From the perspective of cognitive psychology, certain forms of learning can only be interpreted as changes in the psychological process, not merely changes in behaviour itself.

p4.original: 约翰·华生（John Watson）曾在1924年夸口道：“给我12个健康的婴儿，让我一手打造一个世界将他们抚养成人，我敢保证，从中随机抽取任何一个人，不论其天赋、爱好、意愿、能力、天职、祖先的种族，我都能将他训练成为我所指定的专业人士——医生、律师、艺术家或商界领袖，没错，甚至是乞丐和小偷。”数十载后，华生的高调论断背后的假定成为构建“瓦尔登湖第二”（Walden Two）社区的基石：养育胜过天性。换言之，在决定我们的行为的因素中，环境占据的权重比遗传更大。
p4.en: John Watson exaggerated in 1924: “Give me 12 healthy babies and let me build a world where they can grow up, and I can assure you that I can train anyone, regardless of their talent, hobby, will, ability, vocation, ancestral race, to be a doctor, lawyer, artist or business leader, even beggar and thief, as I have designated. After dozens of times, the assumption behind Watson's high-profile theory became the cornerstone of the construction of the Walden Two community: nurturing is better than nature. In other words, among the factors that determine our behaviour, the environment occupies a greater weight than genetics.

p5.original: 在“瓦尔登湖第二”社区，居民们能够从事他们感兴趣的任何职业。在闲暇时间里，他们能够做喜欢做的事：听音乐会，躺在草地上，阅读，或者与朋友一起喝咖啡。这里没有犯罪和毒品问题，也没有贪婪的政客。为了获得这样的幸福生活，社区成员必须每天完成4个“工分”的社区工作。（大约4小时的工作，类似于清洁下水道这类令人不愉悦的工作的时间可以短一些，而修剪玫瑰之类的轻松工作的时间会长一些。）追随华生的愿景，“瓦尔登湖第二”社区的缔造者相信，在一个依据心理学原则打造的、为有益社会的行为提供奖赏的环境中，人们可以拥有幸福而充实的人生。为了获得这些益处，社区要做的是改变其分配奖赏的方式。
p5.en: In the community of Lake Walden II, residents are able to pursue any occupation of interest to them. During their leisure time, they can do what they like: listen to concerts, lie on the grass, read, or have coffee with friends. There is no crime or drug problem, nor is there a greedy politician. In order to achieve such a happy life, members of the community have to complete four “points” of community work per day. (About four hours of work, which may be less time-consuming in unwelcome work like cleaning sewers, and longer in light work such as cutting roses. Following Watson's vision, the founders of Lake Walden II believe that people can live happily and fully in an environment based on psychological principles that rewards socially beneficial behaviour. In order to reap these benefits, the community has to change the way it distributes its rewards.

p6.original: 此社区建于何方？仅存于行为主义者B.F.斯金纳（B.F. Skinner）的头脑中。没错，《瓦尔登湖第二》（Walden Two）是斯金纳在1948年所写的一部小说，目的是推销他的理念——行为心理学能够改善人类生活。不过，他所描述的这个神秘微缩社会的图景如此有诱惑力，以至于催生了许多以“瓦尔登湖第二”为蓝本的真实世界社区。
p6.en: Where is this community built? It's in the mind of the behaviorist B.F. Skinner. Indeed, Walden Two is a novel written by Skinner in 1948 to promote his idea that behavioural psychology can improve human life. However, the picture he described of this mystical micro-shrimp society was so tempting that it gave rise to many real world communities that had their own “Lake Walden II”.

p7.original: 没有任何一个基于“瓦尔登湖第二”的真实社区运行得像斯金纳头脑中的那个社区一样好。然而，现实中至少有一个这样的群体——坐落美国在弗吉尼亚州（Virginia）的双子橡树（Twin Oaks）社区——在40多年之后仍然欣欣向荣，不过其大幅修改了斯金纳的愿景（Kincade，1973）。事实上，你可以从这个群体的网站上了解更多信息（Twin Oaks Intentional Community Homepage，2016）。
p7.en: None of the real communities based on Lake Walden II functioned as well as the community in Skinner's mind. However, at least one such group in reality — the Twin Oaks community in the United States of America, located in Virginia — remained flourishing after more than 40 years, although it significantly modified the Skinner vision (Kincade, 1973). In fact, you can find more information on this group’s website (Twin Oaks International Community 2016).

p8.original: 行为主义的命运也不尽如斯金纳所料。尽管行为主义在20世纪的大部分时间里主导着心理学，但是它最终随着认知心理学的兴起而衰落。不过，行为主义仍然留下了相当多的遗产，包括令人印象深刻的行为学习理论和用于治疗恐惧和恐怖症等习得性障碍的一系列有价值的疗法。我们将以萨布拉所面临的问题为例来说明行为主义留给了我们什么遗产。
p8.en: The fate of behaviorism is not exactly what Skinner expected. Although behavioralism dominated psychology for most of the twentieth century, it eventually declined with the rise of cognitive psychology. However, behaviouralism continues to leave a considerable legacy, including impressive behavioural learning theories and a valuable range of therapies used to treat acquired disorders such as fear and terror. We will use the problems faced by Sabra as an example of what legacy behaviouralism leaves us.

p9.original: 刚毕业的大学生萨布拉（Sabra）在旧金山（San Francisco）的一家广告公司找到了一份朝思暮想的工作。这份工作既有趣，又有挑战性。萨布拉也与新同事相处甚欢。唯一的问题是，她的上司让她参加即将在夏威夷（Hawaii）召开的会议，她还可以在那儿多度几天假，费用由公司承担。为什么这会是个问题？因为萨布拉害怕飞行。
p9.en: A recently graduated university student, Sabra, found a job in San Francisco at an advertising firm. This job is both interesting and challenging. Sabra is also very happy with his new colleagues. The only problem was that her supervisor had asked her to attend the forthcoming meeting in Hawaii, where she could spend additional days at the company's expense. Why is this a problem? Because Sabra was afraid of flying.

p10.en: This chapter considers the following topics:

p11.original: 假定萨布拉害怕飞行是习得的反应，那么她可以通过学习来解决这个问题吗？如果能，怎样治疗？
p11.en: Suppose Sabra's afraid of flying is an acquired reaction, can she learn to solve this problem? If so, how?

p12.original: 心理治疗中的一种常见程式是“重新体验”那些引发恐惧或其他一些症状的创伤经历。而行为学习疗法不一样，它关注此刻和当下而非过去：治疗师就像是一个教练，教导来访者如何用新的反应去置换那些旧的问题行为。因而，当你考虑如何治疗萨布拉的恐惧时，你也许可以思考如下问题。
p12.en: A common formula in psychotherapy is “re-exposure” of traumatic experiences that give rise to fear or other symptoms. Behavioral learning therapy is different, and it focuses on the present and the present, not the past: therapists are like coaches who teach visitors how to replace old problem behaviour with new responses. So, when you think about how to treat Sabra's fears, you might think about the following.

p13.original: 对于像萨布拉一样恐惧飞行的人，我们期待看到哪些问题行为？
p13.en: What are the problems that we expect from people who fear flying like Sabra?

p14.original: 萨布拉可以学会用哪些行为来替换她的恐惧行为？
p14.en: What can Sabra learn to replace her fear?

p16.original: 尽管解决萨布拉的问题要靠学习，但是这里的学习并不是指一般概念上的用功读书。心理学家所定义的学习（learning）概念更为宽泛，指的是个体经历对其行为或心理过程产生持久改变的过程。依据这个定义，萨布拉的飞行训练将会是一种学习，就如同上高尔夫课或阅读本书一样是一种学习体验。
p16.en: While learning is the answer to Sabra's problems, learning here does not mean working on general concepts. The concept of learning, as defined by the psychologist, is broader and refers to the process by which individuals experience lasting changes in their behaviour or psychological processes. According to this definition, flight training in Sabra would be a learning experience, as in golf classes or reading books.

p17.original: 为了避免混淆，定义中有两点需要细化。
p17.en: In order to avoid confusion, two points in the definition need to be refined.

p18.original: 1. 我们要强调的是，学习涉及持久的变化。设想你在医生的诊所里经历了一次特别疼痛的注射，在此过程中，你将针头和疼痛联系起来。结果是，下一次当你需要打针的时候，以及从此以后每次你一看到针头时就会皱眉。这种持久的反应变化涉及学习。相反，当你突然间听到一声巨响会跳起来，类似这样简单的反射性的反应就不属于学习，因为它产生的不是持久的变化，即便其中包含了行为的变化也只是转瞬即逝的反应。
p18.en: 1. We would like to emphasize that learning involves lasting change. It is assumed that you have experienced a particularly painful injection in a doctor's clinic, in which you have linked needles to pain. The result is that the next time you need an injection, and every time you see a needle from now on, you frown. This lasting response change involves learning. On the contrary, when you suddenly hear a loud sound that jumps up, a simple reaction like this is not learning, because it does not produce lasting change, even if it includes behavioural change, it is a instantaneous reaction.

p19.original: 2. 学习影响着行为（behavior）或心理过程（mental processses）。在上述注射的例子中，我们很容易发现学习怎样影响行为，而对于学习如何影响心理过程则很难察觉。例如，你将如何分辨实验室中的一只大鼠仅仅是记住了穿越迷宫所需的行为（向右，然后向左，再向右……），还是循着迷宫的某种心理意象，就像你循着地图一样？（不过，即便大鼠确实在头脑中进行过思考，我们为什么要关心它在想什么？）让我们通过思考关于心理过程的那些争议，更深入地探索学习的定义。
p19.en: 2. Learning influences behaviour (behavior) or psychological processes (mental processes). In the case of injections mentioned above, it is easy to see how learning affects behaviour, and it is difficult to see how learning affects psychological processes. How, for example, will you distinguish between a rat in a lab who simply remembers the behavior required to cross the maze (to the right, then to the left, then to the right...), or some psychological impression of the maze, just like you follow the map? (However, even though rats do think in their minds, why do we care what they think? Let us explore in greater depth the definition of learning by thinking about the controversy about the psychological process.

p21.original: 无论是在大鼠中还是在人类中，观察心理过程的问题都涉及行为主义者和认知心理学家之间一场旷日持久的论战。一方面，在超过100年的时间里，行为主义者都坚持认为，心理学只有摒弃主观的心理过程，仅仅聚焦于可观察的刺激和反应，才能成为一门真正的科学。另一方面，认知心理学家则认为，行为主义的观念狭隘，理解学习需要我们去推理不可见的心理过程。接下来，我们将看到这场论战的双方都为增进我们的知识做出了重要贡献。
p21.en: The problem of observing psychological processes, both in rats and in humans, involved a protracted debate between behaviouralists and cognitive psychologists. On the one hand, for more than 100 years, behaviouralists have insisted that psychology can become a true science only if it rejects subjective psychological processes and focuses only on observable incentives and reactions. On the other hand, cognitive psychologists believe that behavioralism is narrow and that understanding learning requires us to deduce an invisible psychological process. Next, we will see an important contribution by both sides to this debate to our knowledge.

p23.original: 不管是行为学习还是认知学习，学习为我们带来了什么？基本上所有的人类活动，从工作、玩耍到与亲友互动都包含着某种形式的学习。没有学习，我们将没有语言，我们将不知道我们的亲友是谁，我们也将对过去没有记忆，对未来没有目标。没有学习，我们只能依赖于简单的反射和有限的固有行为，这些行为有时被称作本能（instinct）。
p23.en: What does learning bring us, whether it be behavioural or cognitive? Essentially all human activities, from work, play and interaction with relatives and friends, include some form of learning. Without learning, we will have no language, we will not know who our relatives and friends are, and we will have no memory of the past and no goals for the future. Without learning, we can rely on simple reflexes and limited inherent behaviour, sometimes called instinct.

p24.original: 这只巨型棱皮龟每年都会“本能地”回到它的出生地去筑巢。虽然这种行为在很大程度上受基因的影响，但类似于潮汐模式的环境线索也发挥了作用。因而，科学家们通常会避免使用术语“本能”，而倾向于使用术语“物种典型行为”。
p24.en: This giant leatherback returns to its place of birth each year “in instinctively” to nest. While this behaviour is largely influenced by genes, environmental clues similar to tidal patterns also work. As a result, scientists usually avoid using the term “in instincts” and prefer the term “specified species behaviour”.

p25.original: 与学习相反，本能行为严重受到基因编码的影响，就像我们所看到的鸟类的迁徙或动物的交配仪式。然而，人类的行为更多受到学习，而非本能的影响。学习使得我们更为灵活快速地适应不断变化的情境和新环境。从这种意义上来说，学习代表着超越本能的进化优势。
p25.en: Contrary to learning, instinctive behaviour is severely affected by genetic coding, as we see birds migrating or animal mating rituals. However, human behaviour is more influenced by learning than instinct. Learning has made us more flexible and responsive to changing circumstances and new circumstances. In this sense, learning represents an evolutionary advantage that transcends instinct.

p26.original: 简单和复杂的学习形式
p26.en: Simple and complex forms of learning

p27.original: 某些形式的学习非常简单。例如，如果你的住地毗邻一条繁忙的街道，你会学会忽略交通噪声。这种学习被称为习惯化（habituation），也就是学习不对刺激做出反应。习惯化发生于所有拥有神经系统的动物之中，下至蠕虫和昆虫，上至人类。它有助于让你集中精力在重要的刺激上，而忽略那些无须注意的刺激，像你坐在椅子上的触感或是空调发出的噪声。
p27.en: Some forms of learning are very simple. For example, if you live near a busy street, you learn to ignore traffic noise. This learning is called habitation, i.e. learning does not respond to stimulation. Customization occurs in all animals with a nervous system, down to worms and insects, up to humans. It helps to focus you on the important stimulus, ignoring the unmindful stimulation, like the touch on your chair or the noise from the air conditioner.

p28.original: 另一种相对简单的学习形式是，相对于新的刺激，我们通常更偏好熟悉的刺激。这种简单暴露效应（mere exposure effect）的发生不需要刺激与愉悦的事物相伴，甚至不需要我们意识到刺激的存在。简单暴露效应可以解释许多广告效应（Zajonc，1968，2001）。它也能解释为什么在工作场所或学校经常见到的人或者至少听过几次的歌曲会吸引我们。
p28.en: Another relatively simple form of learning is that we tend to prefer familiar incentives to new ones. This simple exposure effect does not have to be accompanied by stimulation and pleasure, or even to be aware of the existence of stimulation. Simple exposures can explain many advertising effects (Zajonc, 1968, 2001). It can also explain why people who are often seen in the workplace or in schools, or who have heard songs at least a few times, attract us.

p29.original: 其他类型的学习更加复杂。一种类型是学习两个刺激之间的关联，就像你会将一种特定的香味与用了这种香水的人联系在一起。另一种类型的学习发生在我们将行动与奖赏或惩罚的后果联系在一起，例如，老板的训斥或教授给的成绩A。这两个例子分属两种极为重要的行为学习（behavioral learning）形式，我们分别称之为经典条件反射（classical conditioning）和操作性条件反射（operant conditioning）。
p29.en: Other types of learning are more complex. One type is learning the connection between two irritations, like you'll connect a particular scent to the person who uses the perfume. Another type of learning takes place when we link action to the consequences of reward or punishment, for example, a boss's reprimand or a professor's achievement A. These two examples are in two very important forms of behavioural learning, which we call classic reflection and operational reflection, respectively.

p30.original: 更为复杂的是内在心理过程的研究。认知学习（cognitive learning）关注突然的“灵光闪现”和模仿行为，这需要超越行为学习的理论去解释我们如何解决问题或是儿童在看到他人获得奖赏时为何会去模仿其行为。认知学习致力于解释概念的习得，这是最为复杂的学习形式，也是你读大学期间的学习方式。
p30.en: More complex is the study of the underlying psychological processes. Cognition learning focuses on sudden “smoking” and imitation, which requires going beyond the theory of behaviour learning to explain how we solve problems or why children are imitating their behaviour when they see their people receiving a reward. Cognitive learning is committed to interpreting the concept, which is the most complex form of learning and the way in which you study during your university.

p31.original: 无论简单还是复杂，所有这些类型的学习都能用于帮助萨布拉克服她对飞行的恐惧。并且，它们提供了众多的小诀窍，可以帮助你更高效地学习并享受学习的乐趣。
p31.en: All these types of learning, simple or complex, can be used to help Sabra overcome her fear of flight. And they provide a lot of little tricks that can help you learn and enjoy learning more efficiently.

p32.original: 那么让我们开始吧，就从一种能够解释你的许多个人好恶的行为学习形式开始：一个被称作经典条件反射的概念。
p32.en: So let's start with a form of learning that can explain many of your personal virtues: a concept known as classic retroreflection of conditions.
